chunks.title: Early Experience Paradigm Overview
chunks.summary: Overall introduction showing the Early Experience paradigm as a bridge between Imitation Learning (IL) and Reinforcement Learning (RL), and serving as the entry point into the data construction pipeline.

chunks.title: Expert Dataset Input (D_expert)
chunks.summary: Starting point of the main pipeline, representing offline expert demonstrations D_expert = {(s_i, a_i)} that seed the Early Experience process and later participate in SR training.

chunks.title: Initial LLM Policy and Non-expert Action Sampling
chunks.summary: Module where the initial LLM policy π_0 takes expert states s_i and samples K non-expert actions {a_i^1,...,a_i^K}, introducing RL-style exploration distinct from expert actions.

chunks.title: Environment Execution and Rollout Dataset (D_rollout) Construction
chunks.summary: Environment interaction stage that takes expert and non-expert state–action pairs, rolls them out to future states, and builds rollout triples D_rollout used as early, reward-free supervision.

chunks.title: Early Experience Data Summary
chunks.summary: Visual and textual consolidation of expert and rollout data into a single Early Experience data perspective, bridging static demonstrations and environment-conditioned rollouts before branching into IWM and SR training.

chunks.title: Implicit World Modeling (IWM) Training Branch
chunks.summary: One of the two core Early Experience training branches where the LLM policy implicitly learns environment dynamics by predicting future states s_i^j from (s_i, a_i^j) using NLL loss over future-state tokens.

chunks.title: Self-Reflection (SR) Training Branch
chunks.summary: The second core Early Experience branch that compares expert and non-expert outcomes, uses the LLM to generate natural language reflections c_i^j, constructs D_refl, and performs multi-task training on actions and explanations.

chunks.title: Joint Training and Policy Update
chunks.summary: Integration point where training signals from IWM and SR branches jointly optimize a unified LLM policy π_θ, combining losses for implicit dynamics modeling, expert action prediction, and explanation generation.

chunks.title: Output Policy and IL–RL Fusion
chunks.summary: Final output of the Early Experience-trained policy/agent and its dual role: improved imitation of expert behavior (IL) and enhanced environment interaction for RL, explicitly illustrating the IL–RL bridge.

chunks.title: Global Annotations and Legend
chunks.summary: Auxiliary annotations explaining concepts like reward-free supervision, the meanings of IWM and SR, and visual conventions distinguishing datasets, models, and environment modules across the figure.

nodes.desc: Main introductory text: "Early Experience paradigm: bridging Imitation Learning and Reinforcement Learning via rollout-based early supervision."
Small labeled shape or icon representing the Imitation Learning (IL) side, e.g., tag "IL" or "Expert Supervision".
Small labeled shape or icon representing the Reinforcement Learning (RL) side, e.g., tag "RL" or "Environment Interaction".
Central bridging shape labeled "Early Experience" indicating the framework that connects IL and RL.

Directional arrow annotation from the IL icon and RL icon towards the central Early Experience block, visually emphasizing Early Experience as a bridge between expert supervision and environment interaction.
Dataset container shape labeled "Expert dataset D_expert" representing the collection of expert demonstrations.
Formula-like text: "D_expert = {(s_i, a_i)}" describing the structure of the expert dataset.
Annotation explaining that s_i denotes expert states and a_i denotes corresponding expert actions.
Short descriptive text such as "offline expert demonstrations" characterizing the nature of D_expert.
Arrow or connector annotation indicating that D_expert serves as the starting input to downstream sampling and training modules.
Module box labeled "Initial LLM policy π_0 (pre-trained LLM-based policy)" representing the starting policy used for sampling non-expert actions.
Arrow annotation from expert states s_i in D_expert into the initial LLM policy π_0, indicating that expert states are used as inputs for sampling.
Text describing sampling: "For each s_i, sample K non-expert actions {a_i^1, ..., a_i^K} from π_0."
Annotation or bracket text noting "{a_i^1, ..., a_i^K} ≠ a_i" to emphasize that sampled actions are non-expert actions.
Grouped shape representing the set of K non-expert action candidates {a_i^1, ..., a_i^K} produced by the initial policy for each expert state.
Module box labeled "Environment" representing the simulator or task environment used for rollouts.
Arrow annotation from expert pairs (s_i, a_i) in D_expert to the Environment module, indicating expert action execution resulting in next state s_{i+1}.
Arrow annotation from non-expert pairs (s_i, a_i^j) to the Environment module, indicating execution of non-expert actions to obtain future states s_i^j.
Text describing transition rules: "Expert: (s_i, a_i) → s_{i+1}; Non-expert: (s_i, a_i^j) → s_i^j."
Dataset container labeled "D_rollout" representing rollout triples built from environment interactions.
Formula-like text: "D_rollout = {(s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j)}" specifying the contents of the rollout dataset for non-expert actions.
Annotation such as "future state used as reward-free supervision signal" explaining the role of s_i^j and s_{i+1} as early experience without explicit rewards.
Merged or grouping shape labeled "Early Experience data" that visually encloses or conceptually groups D_expert and D_rollout.
Summary text such as "From static demos to environment-conditioned rollouts" describing the transition in data types.
Optional summary text like "Early Experience data: rollout triples and expert future states" clarifying what constitutes Early Experience data.
Arrow or branching annotation from the Early Experience data group towards the two core method branches: IWM and SR.
Title label inside the branch: "Implicit World Modeling (IWM)".
Input connector shape indicating that the IWM branch uses D_rollout entries (s_i, a_i^j, s_i^j), typically emphasizing (s_i, a_i^j) as inputs and s_i^j as targets.
LLM policy module box labeled "LLM policy π_θ" used in IWM mode to predict future states from current state–action pairs.
Arrow annotation: (s_i, a_i^j) → LLM policy → predicted future state tokens, indicating the prediction flow.
Loss description text such as "minimize −log p_θ(s_i^j | s_i, a_i^j)" or "NLL loss over future state tokens".
Short annotation like "policy internalizes environment dynamics implicitly" explaining the conceptual role of IWM.
Title label inside the branch: "Self-Reflection (SR)".
Input connector or grouping shape representing paired outcomes from expert and non-expert executions: (s_i, a_i) → s_{i+1} and (s_i, a_i^j) → s_i^j.
Comparison module showing the contrast between expert future state s_{i+1} and non-expert future states s_i^j, labeled "compare outcomes" or similar.
LLM explanation generator module, typically the same underlying LLM policy, taking contextual information (s_i, a_i, a_i^j, s_{i+1}, s_i^j) or their comparison as input.
Text describing generated explanations c_i^j: natural language rationales for why expert action a_i is better than non-expert action a_i^j.
Dataset container labeled "D_refl" representing the self-reflection dataset D_refl = {(s_i, a_i^j, c_i^j)}.
Text or arrow annotation indicating that D_refl and D_expert are jointly used to train the LLM policy in a multi-task fashion (action prediction and explanation generation).
Multi-task training description, e.g., "jointly learn expert action prediction and reflection explanation generation from D_expert and D_refl."
Central policy module labeled "LLM Policy π_θ (updated)" or "Early Experience-trained policy" representing the unified policy after joint training.
Text summarizing loss combination, e.g., "jointly optimize L_IWM + L_action + L_expl" or similar notation.
Input arrow annotation from the IWM branch summarizing the contribution of the future-state prediction (NLL) loss to updating π_θ.
Input arrow annotation from the SR branch summarizing the contributions of expert action prediction loss and explanation generation loss to updating π_θ.
Icon or module labeled "Early Experience Policy / LLM Agent" representing the final deployed agent after training.
Arrow and label indicating the IL-oriented outcome: "better imitation of expert actions (IL)."
Arrow and label indicating the RL-oriented outcome: "enhanced environment interaction / sample efficiency for RL."
Summary text such as "bridging IL and RL via early, reward-free rollouts and self-reflection."
Global annotation: "Future states serve as reward-free supervision (early experience)." placed near environment/rollout modules.
Global annotation: "IWM: implicit dynamics, no explicit world model." positioned near the IWM branch.
Global annotation: "SR: natural language rationales for why expert actions are better." positioned near the SR branch.
Legend-style annotation explaining visual conventions for datasets vs model/policy modules vs environment modules (e.g., different border or color styles).
Optional small note clarifying "early experience" as "rollouts collected before reward-based RL, used for supervision" placed in a neutral area of the figure.
